pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Urine darkening to a deep port-wine hue upon light/air exposure (photo-oxidation of porphobilinogen), precipitated by fasting and CYP450-inducing medications (sulfonamides, metoclopramide) presenting as the classic triad of abdominal pain, neuropsychiatric symptoms, and motor neuropathy. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant inborn error of heme biosynthesis caused by a deficiency in porphobilinogen deaminase (PBG-D / hydroxymethylbilane synthase). Fasting, hormonal shifts, or CYP450-inducing xenobiotics trigger upregulation of the rate-limiting enzyme ALAS1. This results in the massive overproduction and accumulation of neurotoxic heme intermediates—namely delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG)—which damage autonomic, peripheral, and central nervous tissue, leading to abdominal pain, autonomic instability, SIADH (hyponatremia), psychosis, and life-threatening neuroparalysis. Definitive management requires urgent IV glucose loading and IV hemin infusion to suppress ALAS1 transcription.
